title: Ingest-to-release runner for community weights: certify, convert, and publish performance profiles
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: Build an automated 'release-runner' job that takes a community weight bundle from intake -> deterministic conversion -> smoke validation -> canonical pin issuance -> performance profile publishing. This runner should be runnable as a CI/CD job and as a periodic conveyor for newly discovered OSS weights.

Scope:
- Ingest manifest v3 validation and provenance stamping (author, source URL, signed checksum).
- Deterministic conversion pipeline using the canonical exporter (layer order normalization, dtype mapping, and optional quantization hints).
- Tokenizer compatibility checks and edge-case normalization (unknown tokens, legacy merges).
- Runtime smoke: KV cache correctness on short/long context, single-stream latency, end-to-end sample outputs for identity/consistency tests.
- Profiling: microbenchmarks for throughput/latency across pre-configured sequence lengths and batch sizes; memory peak and kernel-level timings.
- Canonical pin creation: produce pin artifact (sha256 of normalized artifact + manifest) and publish to model catalog with metadata.
- Publish performance profile to profiles registry and attach to model catalog entry; include rollout recommendations (default pin, quantized variants, and fallback models).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Runner produces identical conversion artifacts across repeated runs (bit-for-bit stable where feasible) for a given input bundle.
2) Smoke validation detects tokenizer mismatches and rejects unless token-mapping metadata included.
3) Performance profiles (latency P50/P95, throughput at batch=1/8/32, memory peak) are published and visible in the catalog UI.
4) Canonical pin created and referenced by catalog entry; rollback metadata present.
5) Canary run (shadow traffic) executes without >1% functional regression on the selected prompt set.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- We will prefer deterministic conversion even if it costs additional processing time to ensure reproducible pins.
- Quantization will be annotated as a separate variant rather than conflating with the canonical pin.
- For early runs, conversion will be single-threaded to avoid non-determinism; a later optimization will add deterministic parallelism.

Implementation milestones:
M1 (spike, 1 week): ingestion manifest v3 schema + provenance stamping prototype.
M2 (conversion core, 2 weeks): deterministic converter CLI + unit tests for 5 model fmt edge cases.
M3 (smoke + kv tests, 1 week): runtime smoke harness integrated into runner.
M4 (profiling & publish, 2 weeks): perf probes and catalog publish API integration.
M5 (canary & docs, 1 week): shadow traffic canary and runbook + developer docs.

Risks:
- Tokenizer mismatches across community checkpoints (mitigation: require mapping or reject).
- Determinism gaps due to library version differences (mitigation: runner container includes pinned toolchain).
- False negatives in smoke tests for generative output variability (mitigation: use structural checks and canonical prompts).

Monitoring / telemetry: ingest.metrics (ingest_success, ingest_fail_reason), conversion.metrics (duration_ms, delta_bytes), profiling.artifacts (p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_tps), catalog.publish.events. All artifacts should record provenance and the runner job id.

comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha G: Spike completed: manifest v3 prototype accepts git+url and s3 sources. Deterministic stamping approach uses sorted key ordering and SHA256. Found early tokenizer instability in community-bert-3b checkpoint.
2025-02-18 - Marcus L: Decided on conversion CLI name 'rwd-convert' and to emit a conversion.summary.json that includes layer map, dtype changes, and quantization hints.

2025-02-25 - Sofia R (runtime): Integration note - deterministic single-threaded export reduces throughput by ~20% but gives stable pins. Plan to gate parallelization behind a 'deterministic=true' flag.
2025-03-05 - Eng-qa: Profiling run for 3 community models: observed 12% throughput regression on int8 path vs baseline; filed follow-up ENG-762489 to instrument kernel selection heuristics.
2025-03-10 - PM (Liam Chen): Added acceptance criteria to require performance profile publication and catalog visibility before pin is considered GA-ready.
2025-03-14 - Marcus L: Canary executed (shadow): 5k requests, prompt set 'canary-lite-v2'. No functional regressions; small latency bump under batch=32 on one GPU type. Logged for follow-up tuning.
2025-03-18 - Aisha G: Runner CI job merged to release branch; running nightly on inbound community feeds. Next: finalize runbook and add signed artifact storage.
